cohort: Pregnant women in Australia with significant kidney disease, including acute kidney injury, advanced chronic kidney disease, dialysis dependence, or a kidney transplant.
finding: Women with significant kidney disease in pregnancy experienced increased adverse events, including pre-eclampsia (21.7%) and preterm birth (60.9%), and showed high rates of interventions such as aspirin use (82.6%), antihypertensive use (73.9%), indwelling catheters for labour/delivery (65.2%), and blood transfusions (21.7%).
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was common among women with significant kidney disease in pregnancy, occurring in 60.9% of cases.
